statement: Gamer-developers want to talk to Claude Code during active gameplay, in the middle of a match, without leaving the game.
falsifier: If most interviewees describe using Claudictive, or wanting to, only outside active play, or say mid-match use is impractical, this hypothesis is false.
criterion: We are right if at least 6 of 12 interviewees describe a concrete moment in active play when they used, or would use, Claudictive.

statement: Voice input is the feature that will drive adoption: typing is the main barrier to using Claudictive in-game.
falsifier: If fewer than half of interviewees name typing as a barrier, or those who ask for voice also say it would clash with team voice chat, this hypothesis is false.
criterion: We are right if at least 6 of 12 raise voice or typing friction as the reason they use Claudictive less.

statement: Beta usage is low because features are missing; shipping the most-requested features (themes, a smaller window, voice) will raise weekly usage.
falsifier: If interviewees attribute their low usage to something other than missing features, this hypothesis is false.
criterion: We are right if at least 6 of 12 tie their low usage to a specific missing feature.

statement: Gamer-developers will pay about 5 USD a month for Claudictive on top of their Claude subscription.
falsifier: If most interviewees name a price below 3 USD, or make paying conditional on an employer, this hypothesis is false.
criterion: We are right if at least 6 of 12 name 5 USD a month or more without being prompted with a number.
